title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers
items.content_text: Becoming a programmer was, for me, a compromise. Midway through my junior year of college, it became clear that, as an international student from Korea, I likely wouldn’t be able to stay long after graduation unless I changed my major from philosophy to a STEM field that made me eligible for a visa extension. items.title: Trump hosts crypto traders as demand for his meme coin fades
items.content_text: Former U.S. President Donald Trump hosted a crypto investor reception at his Northern Virginia golf club, aiming to re-engage high-net-worth holders and revive the market interest in his meme coins. Trump explicitly called for Congress to enact a federal regulatory framework for digital assets, attempting to align his political agenda with the industry's push for legal clarity.

items.title: Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate
items.content_text: Researchers at the Academy of Military Science in Beijing warn that the U.S. integration of AI into nuclear decision-making could compress response times from 15-30 minutes to under 90 seconds. This capability sparks concerns that U.S. forces may achieve superior precision in detecting and neutralizing Chinese nuclear assets, thereby undermining Beijing's second-strike deterrence.

items.title: Governors Call for Federal AI Rules Without Sidelining States
items.content_text: California Governor Gavin Newsom released a framework for AI governance, proposing baseline safety standards, mandatory third-party audits, emergency shutdown authorities, and limits on recursive self-improvement. The initiative aims to fill federal regulatory voids by imposing legal oversight on AI models with extreme catastrophic risk potential.

items.title: Amazon’s AI resistance: workers ready for battle over data centres
items.content_text: Tech company's plans for rapid expansion face opposition from the public and its own employees

items.title: Boston-based Aevius, whose foundation models analyze patient health using medical records, imaging, and other data, raised a $22M seed led by Insight Partners (Katherine Davis/Axios)
items.content_text: Clinical intelligence startup Aevius has raised $22 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners. The founding team, leveraging their successful track record in selling clinical AI assets to Big Pharma, will focus on building foundation models that analyze EHRs, medical imaging, and multi-modal health data.

items.title: Ant Group Bets on Simplexity to Thrive in China's Humanoid Race
items.content_text: Simplexity Robotics announced that it has received $100 million led by new investor Ant Group Co., Ltd. on November 23, 2026. The company issued convertible preferred shares in the transaction. The transaction includes participation from returning investors Alibaba Group Holding Limited, HongShan Capital Advisors Limited, Tencent Holdings Limited and BlueRun Investment Consulting (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. items.title: Compute Desk, which is building capital markets infrastructure to price, trade, hedge, and clear compute, raised a $45M seed round led by Lightspeed (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
items.content_text: Compute Desk raised $45 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Led by CEO Andrawes Bahou, the startup aims to build capital markets infrastructure to turn compute into a tradable, hedgeable asset, addressing the growing financialization of AI hardware resources.

items.title: Trump’s AI Chip Crackdown Inflicts Collateral Damage Across Asia
items.content_text: China has warned that it will take action to defend its interests after US President Donald Trump's administration introduced tougher restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, escalating tensions over technology access just as the two countries prepare for high-level talks.The measures could also disrupt Southeast Asia's rapidly expanding technology industry, where billions of dollars are being invested in data centres powered by American-made processors.On Monday, 16 November

items.title: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
items.content_text: London-based legal tech firm Alecto raised $20 million in a seed round led by Insight Partners. Founded by Will Rice, the firm aims to leverage AI to automate complex property conveyancing tasks in the UK, challenging traditional hourly billing models to improve transparency and consumer outcomes by 2027.

items.title: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating (Kim Woo-young/CHOSUNBIZ)
items.content_text: Private equity firm MBK Partners has signed a tender offer agreement to take Japanese digital pen technology firm Wacom private in a deal valued at approximately 1.16 trillion yen. Samsung Electronics, a key strategic partner, will participate by tendering its current stake and reinvesting in the acquiring entity, retaining a roughly 6.3% stake to ensure ongoing technological collaboration.

items.title: Arva AI, which builds AI agents for banks' financial-crime compliance teams and counts Wise as a customer, raised a $20M Series A led by Arthur Ventures (Ryan Lawler/Axios)
items.content_text: Arva AI has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Arthur Ventures to advance its AI agent-based compliance automation for the banking sector. The company focuses on streamlining financial crime compliance reviews to minimize human error and operational latency.

items.title: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay
items.content_text: BILL Holdings has reached a definitive agreement to be taken private in an all-cash transaction led by TPG, with a total valuation of approximately $6 billion, involving a minority stake from Corpay. Upon closure in the first half of 2027, BILL will delist from public exchanges, with TPG acquiring a majority interest to integrate BILL’s financial operations with existing payment capabilities.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Claude Fable 5.2 hands-on: nearly tied on three custom accounting, coding, and data tasks, but Fable used far more tokens and cost 5x+ as much (Jessica Wachtel/The New Stack)
items.content_text: Hands-on testing shows that OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 deliver near-identical performance across accounting, coding, and data tasks. However, Claude Fable 5.2 exhibits significantly higher token consumption, resulting in inference costs more than five times higher than its competitor.

items.title: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)
items.content_text: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as acting national cyber director to address escalating cyber threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities while awaiting Senate confirmation of Kirsten A. Davies. This move centralizes oversight to ensure policy cohesion during the transitional period.

items.title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei defended their $900 billion AI infrastructure commitments ahead of their IPO, emphasizing a balanced approach between rapid growth and responsible AI development. The founders reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining an atypical organizational culture while scaling computing resources.

items.title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
items.content_text: Two years before she pulled off the largest public offering of all time, Daniela Amodei gathered everyone at Anthropic in a 16-acre garden on a sweltering fall day near the Santa Cruz mountains. The AI company now with a market value of roughly $1.18 trillion was at the time still a young startup that Amodei and her big brother, Dario, had co-founded with five friends. items.title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
items.content_text: U.S. intelligence reports reveal that Alice Huang, a central figure in the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, maintained consistent contact with Chinese Ministry of State Security officers from spring 2025 through autumn 2024. Investigations indicate that she and her business associate, Kang Wei, utilized their company, Megaspeed, to create a supply chain network that diverted advanced Nvidia chips to Southeast Asian data centers and potentially smuggled restricted hardware into China.

items.title: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently hosted briefings for academics and think tank fellows to showcase how the company's 'AI constitution' guides model behavior. The firm holds a deterministic view that AI will soon surpass human intelligence, prioritizing moral alignment as a core mechanism to mitigate systemic risks.

items.title: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future
items.content_text: SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters. items.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
items.content_text: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that recent outages in aviation and banking systems underscore systemic infrastructure fragility. They emphasized that AI adoption has lowered the barrier for attackers to identify code vulnerabilities, leading to an increased frequency of cyber threats against government and commercial targets.

items.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
items.content_text: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Americans should expect intermittent service outages as government and critical infrastructure undergo systemic upgrades for AI integration. Recent technology disruptions, including those affecting Microsoft Outlook and air travel, have been attributed to network capacity patches rather than AI-related cyberattacks.

items.title: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.content_text: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded a thorough investigation into the supply chain pathways and compliance failures regarding the unauthorized shipment of Nvidia’s advanced chips to China. Following a scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang and alleged Chinese intelligence assets, Huang is scheduled to testify at a closed-door House hearing on December 1st to address whether the non-compliance was a result of internal malice or systematic failure.

items.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.content_text: Edmund McMillen and Nicalis, Inc. integrated AI-generated music containing Suno metadata into 'The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus', violating Valve's mandatory disclosure policy for generative AI and triggering a review-bombing campaign on Steam. Nicalis has since removed the files via a patch, while McMillen issued an apology claiming no prior knowledge of the assets.

items.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
items.content_text: Business Recorder • 22 Nov 2026, 5:00 PM PKT • 1 min read Business Recorder reported that Anthropic’s IPO, which took place on Thursday, raised more than half a billion dollars in underwriting fees but drew complaints from some bankers about the way it was run. The offering surpassed SpaceX’s June listing, and bankers cited a compressed timetable, late changes, delayed financial projections and rushed approvals. items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.content_text: In a simulated software development environment featuring project boards, chat logs, and collaborative workflows, leading models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 achieved a task completion rate of less than 10%. The findings highlight a critical performance gap between high scores on isolated code benchmarks and the requirements of complex, collaborative system engineering.

items.title: The Internet Broke Our Taste. Will A.I. Destroy It for Good?
items.content_text: Silicon Valley is increasingly defining 'taste' as the ultimate human moat against generative AI's algorithmic slop. The current industry debate centers on whether aesthetic judgment is merely a pattern-matching exercise achievable by LLMs, or a uniquely human cognitive capability that determines future market valuation of creative output.

items.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
items.content_text: Perplexity has launched the Monitor API, allowing developers to define monitoring goals via natural language for periodic scanning of specific web pages or global information. The service integrates a decision model to filter out noise, pushing verified updates via webhooks only when findings meet predefined criteria for relevance, credibility, and novelty.

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.content_text: AI research evaluation firm METR reports that large models are closing the gap with human experts in coding and computational tasks, with the complexity of autonomous tasks they can handle doubling every 3.6 months. METR warns that current evaluation environments consistently overestimate model performance for real-world scenarios, and if this trajectory continues, models are projected to reach a 50% success rate on 200-hour complex tasks by July 2027, potentially exceeding human capacity to monitor catastrophic risks.

items.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
items.content_text: A new wave of hardware customization, termed 'vibe-coding,' is emerging as developers utilize large language models like Claude Code and Codex to simplify low-level hardware configuration. By automating interactions such as modifying Android TV interfaces and bypassing bloatware via USB debugging, this trend is significantly lowering the barrier for end-user control over proprietary hardware, fueling a grassroots movement for open-device ecosystems.
